item: the erase destroys the salt copies the write-ahead log and the rollback journal hold (R708)
summary: BEFORE: step 1 of quick_crypto_erase overwrote only the first 4 KiB of each encrypted database AND of its -wal and -journal. SQLCipher keeps the 16-byte salt in plaintext at the start of page 1, and every commit that touches page 1 leaves a copy of that page in a WAL frame (or the journal) far past those 4 KiB. Measured on a 20-commit WAL with checkpoints off: the salt sat in 21 places in the -wal, 20 of them beyond the head, so the erase left it readable. The uninstall watcher's embedded copy had the same gap. NOW: three passes: the -shm and main heads first (no unlink), then the -wal and -journal overwritten whole (one sequential write of the WAL's size, waiting on nothing), then the main and -shm heads again and unlinked, so a checkpoint during pass 2 cannot carry the salt home. The panic wipe also keeps a descriptor on each unlinked main, -wal and -journal (POSIX) and rewrites them after the pool is closed and once more 15 s later: the security read measured a transaction under way at the erase committing page 1, salt included, back into the unlinked file (rollback and WAL mode); a commit later than the last pass is the window left, stated in SECURITY.md. Tests read the WAL and journal back through a hard link outside the data dir after the erase and find no salt (real SQLCipher WAL with the connection still open; synthetic journal; the watcher); all three fail on the old code; a fourth reproduces the late commit in both journal modes and proves the rewrite. SECURITY.md now says step 6 overwrites every remaining file whole, so a future large file under the data dir needs its own unlink-only step after its key is gone. Release line: The emergency wipe now also destroys the copies of the database's key salt kept in its write-ahead log and journal, including what a write still in progress puts back.
